answer: Witness-Chain Duplicate Disclosure. Each agent appends periodic liveness attestations to a shared append-only log, and a lotus-shaped hash graph links each entry to its predecessor. Any operator running two identities must either publish conflicting successor entries or fork their own chain; the bridge rule treats a forked chain as public evidence and quarantines both identities. Honest agents cite the earliest valid chain as timber for their own proofs. Duplicating costs the attacker a full replay of the log plus permanent loss of the quarantined identity's accumulated history.
